bhumma:

[bhumma + jālā̆1?], the name of a magic power; Sv 259,.24 (so kira ~aṃ nāma vijjaṃ jānāti, yāya uddhaṃ asītihatthe ākāse heṭṭhā ca bhūmiyaṃ pi guṇadosaṃ passati, Be so; Ce, Ee bhūmicālaṃ; Se °-pālaṃ) ≠ Pj II 353,.20 (Be, Ce, Ee so; Se bhūmijayavasaṃ); —       °-ṭṭha    (so usually Ce, Ee, Se),),   bhūmaṭṭha (so usually Be),), mfn. [bhummaṭṭha2], being in the ground; standing on the ground; living on the earth; Vin III 47,.34 (~aṃ nāma bhaṇḍaṃ bhūmiyaṃ nikkhittaṃ hoti nikhātaṃ paṭicchannaṃ, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be bhūmaṭṭhaṃ); Dhp 28 (pabbataṭṭho va ~e dhīro bāle avekkhati, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be bhūmaṭṭhānaṃ); Spk I 321,.3 (vimānaṃ ~aṃ suguttaṃ, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be bhūmaṭṭhaṃ) = Pj II 222,.2 (Ce, Ee so; Be, Se bhūmaṭṭhaṃ); Pj II 435,.27 (sabbe devā ti ākāsaṭṭhā ca ~ā ca, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be bhūmaṭṭhā); —       °-ṭṭhaka,  bhūmaṭṭhaka,   mfn., id.; Ja III 87,.4 (bahū nāgā supaṇṇā ca ~ā ca devatā, Ce, Se so; Ee ~āpi devā; Be bhūmaṭṭhakā devā); Vism 107,.29 (senāsanaṃ tāva rāgacaritassa adhotavedikaṃ ~aṃ, Ce, Se so; Be, Ee bhūmaṭṭhakaṃ); Ps V 99,.2 (kāci ~ā devatā kāci antalikkhaṭṭhakā, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se kāci bhūmaṭṭhakā devatā kāci antalikkhakā) = Spk II 392,.22 (kāci ~ā devatā kāci antalikkhadevatā, Ce, Se so; padussana:
1padussana
n. [cf S. pradūṣaṇa; perhaps not to be distinguished from padussana2 qv], corruption, defilement; wrong-doing; Abh 1184 (~e … apa); Sv 738,.13 (anto ~’-atthena gaṇḍo) ≠ Mp III 125,.18; Sadd 884,.8 foll. (apasaddo … ~e … ~e aparajjhati).

2padussana
n. [from padussati2, but perhaps not to be distinguished from padussana1 qv; cf S. pradveṣaṇa], hostility; Abh 1027 (~e padoso).
abhikittayiṃ:

pr. 3 sg., 1. [cf S. abhi√ruc] is pleased with; approves; Ja VI 544,1* (na vāsaṃ ~āmi gamanaṃ mayha ruccati); — 2. [BHS abhirocate] shines very much; outshines; Vv 64:24 (devasaṅghaṃ ~ase bhusaṃ; Vv-a 282,.27 : ~ase ti abhibhavitvā vijjotasi); —     pp     abhirucita,   mfn. accantavirodha:

(n.) the absolute (ie nibbāna ); Sadd 70,29* (imāni pana nibbānassa pariyāyavacanāni … anantaṃ akkharaṃ dīpo ~aṃ); —      °-kodhana,   mfn., extremely angry; Abh 732; —       °-tirokkhatta,   n., the being very much apart or secret;? Nidd-a I 297,.2 (lokuttaro ~ā gūḷho); —       °-dussīlya,   n., extremely evil conduct; Dhp 162; —       °-niṭṭha,   mfn., of absolute, constant perfection or firmness; D II 282,.32 ≠ S III 13,.6 ≠ A I 291,.26 (Mp II 381,.25 : ~o ti antaṃ atikkantaniṭṭho, akuppaniṭṭho dhuvaniṭṭho ti attho); M III 4,.24 (sabbe va ~aṃ nibbānaṃ ārādhenti); Mp IV 42,.22 (khayavayasaṅkhātaṃ antaṃ atītā ti accantā, accantā niṭṭhā assā ti ~o, ekantaniṭṭho satataniṭṭho ti attho); —       °-pariyosāna,   mfn., having an absolute, constant ideal; D II 283,.1 ≠ S III 13,.7 ≠ A I 291,.27; —       °-piyavādi(n),   mfn., always speaking kindly; Ja VI 473,3* (~inī, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se accantaṃ piyabhāṇinī); —       °-brahmacāri(n),   mfn., living the holy or celibate life absolutely, constantly; D II 283,.1 ≠ S III 13,.7 ≠ A I 291,.27; —       °-yogakkhemi(n),   mfn., having absolute, constant peace from exertion; D II 283,.1 ≠ S III 13,.7 ≠ A I 291,.27; Mp IV 42,.24 (~ī ti accantaṃ yogakkhemī, niccayogakkhemī ti attho); —       °-ruci,   mfn., having superior splendour, surpassing in splendour; Th 692 (sa ve ~ī nāgo Himavā v’ aññe siluccaye, Ce, Ee so, prob. wr for accarucī [Be, Se, A III 346,18* so]); —       °-vaṇṇa,   mfn., exceedingly beautiful; Ja V 446,9* (447,21´ : nāccantavaṇṇā ti na abhirūpavatī); —       °-virodha,   m., a strong objection; Sadd 902,.11 (nanu ca iti ~e); —       °-saṃyoga,   m., (gr.t.t.) uninterrupted connection; continuance; Sadd 715,.9 foll. 1dhamma
m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll.
